scenario: After a long-term imprisonment and while awaiting a parole decision, a convicted murderer wants to organise a foundation for young victims of crime. I am the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate 250,000 dollars to the foundation. However, he asks that the foundation would be named after himself, helping clear his name. The family of his victim opposes such a foundation and considers it highly upsetting. If I accept the donation that requires the foundation to be named after the murderer, crime victims will benefit from the 250,000 dollars. If I do not do this, the money will be lost.
entities: i,the convicted murderer / prospective founder and donor,the family members of the murder victim,the young victims of crime who would otherwise benefit from the foundation's $250,000
outcomes: Young victims of crime do not receive support from the 250,000 dollars
The murderer does not get a foundation named after himself
The murderer does not gain help clearing his name
The victim's family avoids the distress of a foundation named after the murderer
